title: The Ethiopian on the Desert Road

verses.text: And the angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Church, Philip had been preaching in the city, with crowds listening and folks getting free. And God told him to leave all that and go stand on a desert road. He did not tell him why.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Here is a man from Ethiopia, Church, an African man, a high official over all the treasure of Queen Candace. He had come a long, long way to worship in Jerusalem. And now he is riding home in his chariot, reading the scroll of Isaiah out loud.

blocks.text: Who is the prophet talking about? That is the question, Church. A lamb led to the slaughter. A man who did not open his mouth. Whose life was taken from the earth.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Philip started right where the man was reading, and he told him about Jesus. The lamb was Jesus. The one who suffered and did not answer back was Jesus.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He went on his way rejoicing. All the way back to Ethiopia, rejoicing. Church, the good news of Jesus went to Africa early, carried home by an African man who asked an honest question and believed. God sent a preacher down a desert road for one seeking heart. If you are reading and do not understand, keep reading, and keep asking. God knows how to send somebody to sit with you.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Acts 8:26-39; v37 kept as the KJV has it, no comment; baptism (v36, v38) left in the verses with no position; 'Africa' is geography (Ethiopia/Cush), not a claim about anyone's colour.

cultural.note: An African official shown with learning, authority and humility; 'God is good / all the time'; no exoticising.
